info.name: Opportunity Portal — Frontend Integration
info.description:
APIs the frontend needs for login, password management, profile, and estimates. All endpoints (except Login/Forgot Password/Reset Password) require a JWT — put it in the `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.

## Authentication flow
1. `POST /auth/login` with email + password → returns `{ token, user, mustChangePassword }`.
2. Store `token` (e.g. in memory / secure storage) and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every subsequent request.
3. `mustChangePassword: true` means this is a NetSuite-synced account still on its default password. This is informational only — the API does NOT block access because of it — but the UI should still prompt the user to change it (e.g. a banner or a redirect to a change-password screen), since it means they're using a shared default password (`password@123`).
4. There is no public sign-up. Every login account is either synced automatically from NetSuite (when an employee record is created there) or created manually by an admin.

## Test credentials (local/dev only)
```
email:    frontend.tester@opportunityportal.test
password: password@123
```
This account has no real NetSuite employee data behind it (job title, department, etc. will be null in Profile), and no estimates are attached to it (`netsuiteInternalId: "800001"` doesn't match any real Sales Rep / Ops Partner / Product Developer / creator on any estimate), so estimate lists will come back empty for it. It's meant for exercising the auth flow itself. Ask backend for a test identity tied to real estimate data if you need to see non-empty estimate results.

## Estimate access control
`GET /estimates`, `/estimates/search`, `/estimates/document-numbers`, and `/estimates/:id` all automatically filter to only what the logged-in user is authorized to see: estimates they created, or where they're the Sales Rep, an Ops Partner, or a Product Developer (matched via their NetSuite Internal ID). There's no query param to control this — it's entirely driven by the JWT. The frontend doesn't need to do anything extra here beyond sending the token; just be aware an empty result can be correct behavior, not a bug.

## Base URL
Set `{{baseUrl}}` (collection variable, top of the Variables tab) to wherever the backend is running — defaults to `http://localhost:3000`.

request.description:
Response shape:
```
{
  "token": "<jwt>",
  "user": { "id": number, "email": string, "role": string, "netsuiteInternalId": string | null },
  "mustChangePassword": boolean
}
```
This request's test script auto-saves `token` into the collection variable `{{token}}`, so every other request in this collection just works after you run this once. 401 with `{"code":"UNAUTHORIZED", "message":"Invalid credentials"}` means wrong email/password or the account is inactive.

Response: `{ id, email, firstName, lastName, role, mustChangePassword }`. Lightweight — use this if you just need to confirm the token is valid / get basic identity, without the NetSuite employee join Profile does.

Requires the user's current password (min 8 chars for the new one). On success: `{ "message": "Password changed successfully" }` and `mustChangePassword` flips to `false` server-side — the OLD token in hand still carries the stale `mustChangePassword: true` claim until the user logs in again or hits Refresh Token, since JWTs are immutable once issued. 401 with `"Current password is incorrect"` on a wrong current password.

Always returns `200` with a generic message (`"If an account with that email exists, a password reset link has been sent."`) — by design, it never reveals whether the email exists, so don't treat this response as confirmation an email was actually sent.

The email contains a link shaped like `{FRONTEND_URL}/reset-password?token=<longToken>`. **The frontend needs a route at that path** which reads the `token` query param and lets the user set a new password there — that page then calls Reset Password below with the token and the new password.

`token` is the value from the query param in the emailed reset link (`?token=...`), not anything the frontend generates. Single-use and time-limited (currently configured server-side, ask backend for the exact TTL). On success: `{ "message": "Password reset successfully" }`. On an invalid/expired/already-used token: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` — `"Invalid or expired reset link"`. The frontend should show that message and let the user request a new link (re-run Forgot Password).
Re-signs a fresh token reflecting the user's current DB state (e.g. an up-to-date `mustChangePassword` after Change Password, without forcing a full re-login). Requires a still-valid existing token.

query.description: free-text match on project name / customer PO
e.g. draft, submitted, approved, otb, closed_won, closed_lost

request.description: Simple paginated list, automatically scoped to what this user can see (see collection description). Response: `{ data: [...], pagination: { page, limit, total } }`.

query.description: pass to get one full estimate (with line items/freight groups) instead of a list
comma-separated local account_managers ids (NOT NetSuite ids)

request.description: The full-featured list view (used by the main Estimates grid). All the *Id filters here take LOCAL database ids (from the dropdown/master-data endpoints), not NetSuite internal ids — don't confuse these with the identity-based access control, which is separate and automatic. Response includes line items, freight groups, and creative requests per estimate.
Lightweight list for a document-number picker/dropdown — same filters and access scoping as Search Estimates, but returns just `{ id, documentNumber, projectName, customerName, status }` per row.

Full estimate detail with line items, freight groups, quotes, and creative requests. Replace `1` with a real id. Returns `404` both when the id truly doesn't exist AND when it exists but this user isn't authorized to see it — the frontend can't distinguish these cases, and shouldn't try to (that's intentional, to avoid confirming an estimate's existence to someone who shouldn't see it).
